subject: Unit-econ sensitivity & runway-friendly pilot — post-call recap
messages:
From: Alex Hill <alex.hill@slateledger.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@slateledger.com
Date: 2026-11-01T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick cost discussion

Thanks for the call earlier — quick follow-up from my side. High level: we liked the approach but need a tighter view on unit economics before we get procurement involved. Main constraints: (1) Q1 pilot budget is ~$60k (hardware + software), (2) latency target ~120ms p50 for customer-facing experience, (3) we expect ~300k inference tokens/month initially, with spikes during monthly billing cycles.

Can you put together a concise sensitivity table showing: cost/token at current profile, cost/token if we enable batching (2x/4x), and cost with prefix/KV cache for repeat sessions? Also show rough ROI if we cut per-interaction cost by 40% (how many saved ops / revenue lift assumptions needed to pay for Redwood). I'd prefer a single-slide summary + a spreadsheet model.

Finally, procurement will want a one-page pilot SOW and a rough timeline to approval. Can you send both by EOD Tuesday PST?

—Alex
Alex Hill
Head of ML Engineering, SlateLedger

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hill <alex.hill@slateledger.com>, procurement@slateledger.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T17:18:00-07:00
Subject: Unit-econ sensitivity & pilot SOW — follow-up (recap + next steps)

Alex / Sue — thanks again for the call. Recap below plus next steps / asks so everyone is aligned.

Recap of pain & goals:
- Primary pain: current inference cost is a blocker to wide rollout; need predictable unit economics to secure Q1 pilot budget (~$60k).
- Product goal: customer-facing latency target ~120ms p50; willing to accept modest tail variance for cost savings.
- Usage: initial footprint ~300k tokens/month with concentrated monthly spikes.

What we committed to deliver (by Tue EOD PST):
1) One-slide executive summary: headline cost per 1k tokens (baseline), and scenarios for 2x and 4x batching and a KV/prefix cache case.
2) Spreadsheet model: line items (tokens, per-token compute, gateway overhead, cache hit assumptions, batching efficiency curves, reserved vs burst pricing) and sensitivity slider cells.
3) Pilot SOW draft (1 page): objectives, success metrics, duration (6 weeks), Redwood responsibilities, SlateLedger responsibilities, acceptance criteria, estimated cost envelope.
4) Optional: quick decision tree showing when to enable quantized variants vs standard models based on quality thresholds.

Key assumptions we will model (please confirm or correct):
- Baseline model: open-llm-aligned ~13B fp16-like performance; baseline throughput used for per-token compute.
- Batching 2x -> conservative 25% per-token cost reduction; 4x -> 40% reduction (varies by latency SLO).
- KV cache hit rate assumption: 30% for repeat sessions (we'll show 10%/30%/50% scenarios).
- Pilot capacity: reserved pool for peak windows + autoscale for off-peak.

Immediate asks from SlateLedger:
- Confirm whether pilot must run in your VPC (private) or hosted Redwood is acceptable for the PoC.
- Any compliance docs required upfront (SOC2-in-progress is fine; procurement will ask for evidence).

Next meeting: propose Wed 11/3 10:00am PT to review the slide + spreadsheet — let me know if that works.

Attachments: pilot-budget-model.xlsx (will send), slateledger-pilot-sow-draft.pdf (attached).

Thanks — I'm copying Ben and Marissa who will own the budget model and SOW respectively.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hill <alex.hill@slateledger.com>, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unit-econ sensitivity & pilot SOW — model assumptions

Alex — quick note on the model assumptions before we finalize:
- I'll attach a small workbook with a baseline (1.0x) throughput cost using our deduped kernel selection. For clarity I'll show: tokens/sec, effective GPU-hours, price/GPU-hour (reserved vs on-demand), and resulting cost/token.
- Batching: we'll present latency vs cost curves. At p50 120ms we believe 2x batching is realistic without breaking the SLO for typical SlateLedger request sizes; 4x can be offered as a peak-window optimization.
- Cache: KV/prefix cache will show diminishing returns after ~40% hit-rate for your traffic shape; we will graph marginal savings.
- Quality/quantization: we will flag the risk of aggressive quantization impacting edge-case correctness — include a QA checklist for prompt-level evals.

Deliverables I'll upload to the shared Drive folder and attach the spreadsheet to the SOW email.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
